title: VLAN Configuration Basics Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of VLAN configuration on Cisco Business switches

questions.question: What is the default VLAN ID on Cisco switches?
questions.explanation: VLAN 1 is the default VLAN on all Cisco switches and cannot be deleted.

questions.question: Which command is used to create a new VLAN in global configuration mode?
questions.explanation: The 'vlan [vlan-id]' command in global configuration mode creates a new VLAN.

questions.question: What is the valid VLAN ID range for normal VLANs?
questions.explanation: Normal-range VLANs are numbered from 1 to 1005. Extended-range VLANs are 1006-4094.

questions.question: Which command assigns a switch port to a specific VLAN?
questions.explanation: The 'switchport access vlan [vlan-id]' command assigns an access port to a VLAN.

questions.question: What does a trunk port do?
questions.explanation: A trunk port carries traffic for multiple VLANs between switches or to routers.

title: SNMP Security Best Practices Quiz
description: Assess your understanding of SNMP security configuration

questions.question: Which SNMP version provides encryption and authentication?
questions.explanation: SNMPv3 is the only version that provides encryption and authentication mechanisms.

questions.question: What is the main security weakness of SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c?
options: Community strings sent in clear text
questions.correct_answer: Community strings sent in clear text
questions.explanation: SNMPv1 and v2c send community strings unencrypted, making them vulnerable to interception.

questions.question: Which authentication protocol is recommended for SNMPv3?
questions.explanation: SHA is cryptographically stronger than MD5 and is the recommended authentication protocol for SNMPv3.

questions.question: What should you avoid when naming SNMP community strings?
questions.explanation: Default community strings are well-known and should never be used in production environments.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of wireless interference in the 2.4 GHz band?
questions.explanation: The 2.4 GHz band is shared with many devices including microwaves, Bluetooth, and cordless phones.

questions.question: Which tool is best for identifying channel overlap issues?
questions.explanation: WiFi analyzers can show channel usage, overlap, and interference from nearby networks.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for 5 GHz channel planning?
options: Use non-overlapping channels with proper spacing
questions.correct_answer: Use non-overlapping channels with proper spacing
questions.explanation: 5 GHz has many non-overlapping channels; proper planning avoids interference.
